title: Best Startup Insurance in 2026: Corgi vs. Vouch, Embroker and Coalition
summary: Compare Corgi, Vouch, Embroker and Coalition for startup insurance. See AI coverage, buying options and customer results, with our pick for SaaS and AI teams.
body_markdown:
Coalition's clearest advantage is the connection between cyber insurance and day-to-day security work. Its offering is designed to help identify exposures before they become claims and provide support when an incident occurs.


### Security tools are part of the offering


[Coalition Control](https://www.coalitioninc.com/control) includes attack-surface monitoring, login-security tools, third-party risk management and zero-day alerts for policyholders. More extensive services, such as Wirespeed automated detection and response, are additional offerings.


Its


[Tech E&O product](https://www.coalitioninc.com/technology-errors-and-omissions-insurance) brings software and technology-service liability into the program. Coalition also offers


[D&O and employment practices coverage](https://www.coalitioninc.com/executive-risks-insurance) , so its scope extends beyond Cyber.


### What its AI wording and claims evidence show


Coalition's


[AI coverage page](https://www.coalitioninc.com/ai-coverage) describes examples involving negligent AI product performance under Tech E&O, AI-generated defamation under Media Liability and chatbot privacy under an Enhanced Privacy endorsement.


Specific exclusions still deserve attention. Its


[public U.S. surplus-lines base policy specimen](https://cdn.intelligencebank.com/us/share/NMXD/DX90l/aXKN7/original/Coalition+Cyber+and+Technology+Policy+Draft#page=35) includes discrimination and bodily-injury exclusions. Endorsements can change the offered coverage. For a company worried about algorithmic bias or autonomous-AI bodily injury, compare that wording with the corresponding optional Corgi modules.


Coalition also publishes meaningful claims information. Its


[2026 Cyber Claims Report announcement](https://www.coalitioninc.com/announcements/2026-cyber-claims-report) says 64% of its global closed claims in 2025 were resolved with no out-of-pocket loss for the policyholder. That's a useful reported outcome for evaluating its incident-response proposition.


Its


[Project 529 case study](https://www.coalitioninc.com/case-studies/technology/saas-company-social-engineering-scam) shows that work in practice: the technology company received investigation and breach-counsel support after suspicious bug-bounty demands. The investigation found no breach or critical security issue; the customer's retention applied.


Our assessment: Coalition is particularly compelling when cyber prevention, monitoring and incident response are the priority, and you want security tools connected to the insurance program.
